drug_class: Platelet-derived growth factor (topical wound healing agent)
purpose: Becaplermin gel is used to help heal diabetic foot ulcers — those are open sores or wounds on the feet that happen in people with diabetes. It works best when used along with good wound care. It helps wounds that go all the way down to the tissue under the skin and have a good blood supply.
how_it_works: Your body naturally makes proteins called growth factors that tell cells to grow and repair damaged tissue. Becaplermin is a man-made version of one of those proteins. When you apply it to your wound, it helps attract the right cells to the area and signals them to start rebuilding and closing the wound.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is a rash or skin irritation near the wound where you apply the gel. Some people may notice redness, pain, or swelling around the area. These are usually mild and happen right at the application site.
warnings: Important: Studies have suggested that people who use more than 3 tubes of this gel may have a slightly higher risk of developing cancer. Talk to your doctor right away if cancer is a concern for you. Do not use this gel on wounds near any area where you have had cancer. Do not put it in your eyes, mouth, or nose. Keep it away from children. Store it in the refrigerator — do not freeze it.
typical_dosing: Your doctor will tell you exactly how much to use based on the size of your wound. Usually, you apply a thin layer of gel once a day to the clean wound, cover it with a moist dressing, and leave it on for about 12 hours. After 12 hours, rinse the wound gently with saline or water and cover it with a plain moist dressing for the rest of the day. Your dose may change as your wound heals and gets smaller.
